key_insight: EndoCLIP turns routine colonoscopy reports into lesion-level image-text supervision, creating a colonoscopy-specific vision-language foundation model.
clinical_relevance: This could help improve automated lesion recognition and report understanding, potentially reducing the need for task-specific manual annotation in future endoscopy tools.
method: Recovered 125,756 lesion-level image-text pairs from 280,476 routine colonoscopy reports
Trained a colonoscopy vision-language model, EndoCLIP, on paired image and report data
Evaluated retrieval, structured report generation, and six multi-centre classification tasks
evidence_signal: The model outperformed general-purpose and biomedical encoders in zero-shot and linear-probe settings, and its benign-versus-malignant linear probe approached expert endoscopist performance in a blinded study of 12 readers.
watch_item: Because the lesion-to-frame correspondence is progressively recovered from routine reports, performance may depend on report quality and the reliability of that linking step across sites.
paper_title: A report-grounded vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy from 280000 routine reports
